pages.text: Create trains run on their own track network and carry glued-together blocks as cars. You can drive one yourself or hand it a schedule.$(br2)Hold W over any item here to watch its Ponder.

Train Track is its own block, not a vanilla rail. Click a placed track, then another spot, to lay a straight, a curve or a slope in one go. Sprint while connecting for the longest bend that fits. Blocks in your off-hand are paved under the track.
pages.title: Track
Train Track
pages.text: Placed against a Nether portal, track builds a matching line on the other side, so trains can cross dimensions.

A $(thing)Train Station$() is a waypoint on your network. Place it beside a track and open its screen. Assembly Mode builds a train, and scheduled trains stay away while it is on. A train can only be turned back into blocks at a station.
pages.title: Stations
Train Station
pages.text: Use a map on a station to add a labelled marker at that spot. Assembled trains can be nudged onto nearby track with a wrench.

Use $(item)Train Casing$() on a track to place a bogey, the wheel unit a car rides on. Click the track again to cycle designs. Glue blocks on with Super Glue. Every train needs Train Controls, and a second set facing the other way lets it leave a station in either direction.
pages.title: Bogeys and controls
Train Casing
pages.text: Used on a track it places a bogey. Small and large bogeys are available.

pages.title: Train Controls
pages.text: Right-click once assembled to drive. Movement keys steer, the mouse wheel sets top speed, sneak lets go.

A train moves faster if it finds fuel in chests or barrels glued to it. Vault fuel is not burned. Hold space while driving to roll up to a station.$(br2)Track works in unloaded chunks: trains still travel and stop, but on-board machines wait until a player is near.
